request: What did CRS report about Medicare prescription drug price negotiation and its expected savings?

reply.reply:
CRS reported that CBO forecast the Medicare drug negotiation provisions would reduce federal Medicare drug spending by **$25 billion in 2031**. CBO also projected average Part D net prices would be **9% lower** and average Part B prices **8% lower** that year. These are forecasts, not realized savings. (CRS R47872, December 2023, PDF p. 15)

The program authorizes HHS to negotiate prices for certain single-source drugs and biologics covered under Medicare Part B or Part D. (CRS R47872, PDF p. 2)

[See the cited brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-171638-f98c.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified CRS findings give the program's scope and CBO's projected 2031 spending and price effects; the brief explicitly distinguishes forecasts from realized savings.
